method_source.paper: Schoenbach et al., Integration of the TIAGo Robot into Isaac Sim with Mecanum Drive Modeling and Learned S-Curve Velocity Profiles, arXiv:2510.10273v1
method_source.section: III-A, Fig. 3b: each roller collider modeled with six spheres
method_source.paper_cites: Wiedemann et al., ICRA 2024, DOI 10.1109/ICRA57147.2024.10611459 (method origin; full text NOT read)
method_source.paper_claim_scope: computationally cheaper than mesh or low-poly colliders; no speed number or MasterPi evidence is quoted here

values_source.license: AGPL-3.0 (repository). No file is copied; only the six sphere centres and radii below are transcribed.
values_source.used_by: tiago_dual_functional.usd payloads ./wheels/mecanum_wheel.usd for all four wheels; mecanum_wheel.usd payloads roller_link.usd for 15 rollers
values_source.read_with: system usdcat (USDC to ASCII); prims collision_sphere_00..05, physics:approximation=boundingSphere, mesh point radius 50 x xformOp:scale
values_source.friction: PhysicsMaterial dynamic/static 0.8 (same as FUJI value already used by v2)
values_source.units: mecanum_wheel.usd metersPerUnit=1; roller_link.usd layer does not author it. Meters is confirmed by the unit test that compares each radius with the FUJI STL radial profile.

scale_to_masterpi: official MasterPi wheel diameter 0.065 m / TIAGo wheel diameter 0.205 m = 65/205 (same scale as the v2 FUJI mesh)
sphere_axis: all centres lie on the roller hinge axis (local x); same axis as the FUJI STL long axis and the v2 passive hinge
unconfirmed: installed MasterPi roller shape (the 65/205 scaling is a similarity assumption, as for v2)
whether six spheres reproduce mesh traction on MasterPi; decided only by the equivalence table in the experiment README
full text of the ICRA 2024 source paper
